spotlight.title: The lost Sep 6 lead is a real person — Mary Grossman — and she wants a call by tomorrow
spotlight.detail: The four-day “missing lead” now has a name, a state and a deadline: Mary Grossman (NV) asked for an appointment around Sep 11 — tomorrow — and nobody has reached her. The diagnosis also changed today: the watchdog checked the automation directly and it ran successfully, then silently marked her “not worth alerting” — an alert-suppression bug, not the form→sheet wiring flagged 10+ times since Sep 7. Two calls to make today: (1) whether Mary can be contacted at all with compliance still 0/7 and NV outside licensed area, and (2) point the fix at the “alert admin” step, not the sheet.

spotlight.title: Amanda's welcome-email bug is still open — her lead got nothing and still isn't called
spotlight.detail: Frankie's own overnight end-to-end test (lead AMANDA, L-YTCLT0-XC) reached the CRM clean at 04:32Z, but the W1 Lead Ingest run logged “success” while never sending the welcome email — SLA breach, and as of 04:06Z she still hadn't been called by hand. This is the second, distinct break point: the funnel drops leads AFTER capture, not only at the form. Open the W1 run internals — the step that reports success without sending — fix it, and re-submit to prove it, the same way you'll prove the alert-suppression fix.
